sentences.text:
Prasanna Kumar And 3 Others vs Union Of India And 4 Others
on 20 April, 2023
Author: Sunita Agarwal

Bench: Sunita Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 29
Case :- Writ - C No. - 13231 of 2023
Petitioner :- Prasanna Kumar And 3 Others

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent :- Union Of India And 4 Others Counsel for Petitioner :- Manish Kumar Jain

Counsel for Respondent :- A.S.G.I.,Dinesh Kumar Misra,Pranjal Mehrotra Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
Heard Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, appearing on behalf of respondent N.H.A.I. and Sri Dinesh Kumar Misra, learned counsel has put in appearance on behalf of respondent no.1.

The petitioners herein are aggrieved by the inaction of the competent authority namely the respondent no.5/Additional District Magistrate (Land Acquisition), Lalitpur in not making payment under the arbitral award dated 18.11.2020, despite there being an order dated 3rd March, 2023 of the Arbitrator in Execution Case No.10/15-16.

The attention of the court is invited to a letter dated 16th March, 2023 which has been written by the Project Director N.H.A.I. to the Competent Authority/Additional District Magistrate, Finance &
Prasanna Kumar And 3 Others vs Union Of India And 4 Others on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147518789/
1 Revenue (Land Acquisition), Lalipur stating therein that the First Appeal No.747 of 2017 is pending before this Court.
On a pointed query made by the Court, it is admitted by the learned counsel appearing for the N.H.A.I. that the First Appeal No.747 of 2017 filed under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 has been dismissed for want of prosecution on 28.8.2017.
The restoration application for recall of the order dated 28.8.2017 has also been rejected on 29.11.2019 for want of prosecution.
Another restoration application has been filed for recall of the order dated 29.11.2019 which is stated to be pending as on date.
It is, thus, evident that the arbitral award dated 18.11.2020 has been affirmed with the rejection of the application under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act, 1996 filed by the N.H.A.I.

With the dismissal of the First Appeal under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act,
1996, there is no legal impediment in making payment under the award, for the mere fact that the restoration application, that too recall of the order of the dismissal of the restoration application, is pending consideration.

In any case, with the dismissal of the first appeal on 28.8.2017, the communication made by the Project Director about the pendency of the restoration application cannot be reason to deny payment to the petitioners herein.

We, therefore, issue direction to the Competent Authority (Land Acquisition),Lalitpur to proceed with the disbursement of compensation to the petitioners under the arbitral award dated 18.11.2020 in compliance of the order dated 3.3.2023 passed by the Arbitrator/District Magistrate, Lalitpur, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of three weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

It goes without saying that the disbursement of compensation shall be subject to the deposit of adequate security as indicated in the arbitral award dated 18.10.2020 and the order of the Arbitrator/District Magistrate, Lalitpur dated 3.3.2023.
The writ petition is accordingly, allowed.
